before.delivered: I think the main thing we need to do is make the first few seconds feel easier. When I start talking, I don't always have the whole sentence planned out. Sometimes I know what I mean, but the wording takes a second to catch up. That's normal; I don't want every little hesitation preserved forever. I also don't want the cleanup to decide that half of what I said wasn't important. The main thing is keeping the meaning intact. We should probably check the simple cases before we get too excited about the complicated ones. I like the current direction, and I really like having fewer steps between thinking something and writing it down. When I say that something looks like another thing, the word like belongs there. When I say like maybe we should start over, some of those can probably go.
